symptoms: The job fails naming a fully qualified class that is not in the job's own code
The same code runs locally, where the missing jar happens to be on the classpath
The failure appears at the moment the class is first needed, not at submission
likely_causes: The jar that carries the class was never delivered to the classpath
The class comes from a connector or format that the runtime does not bundle
The dependency was declared for the build but not for the runtime
diagnostic_steps: List the jars actually delivered to the job and check whether any of them carries the named class
Read spark.jars and the extra classpath entries from spark.conf_effective, and compare with what the job declares
Confirm whether the class belongs to a connector the runtime is expected to bundle, or to a dependency the job must ship
fixes: Deliver the jar that carries the class to the classpath, through the mechanism the runtime provides
If the class comes from a connector the runtime bundles under a different name, use the runtime's own switch instead of shipping a second copy
unsafe_fixes: Shipping a second copy of a jar the runtime already bundles: it turns an absent class into a duplicated one, and the failure moves rather than disappearing
verification: Re-run the job and exercise the code path that loads the class, not only the submission
rollback: Revert the classpath change. It changes no data, but partial output written by the failed run has to be discarded or reconciled separately
